title: The page's data layer: API, live stream, polling
request: The product's pages must talk to the real server: JSON calls with the request token, live events and polling, while pages not yet wired keep their sample data honestly labelled.
spec: DC.api (JSON, CSRF header from /api/config, one retry when the token is stale), DC.stream (server-sent events), DC.poll; the demo-only shared store removed; the blueprint layer and tours kept. Done when Home loads /api/workspace with no console error and a write after a server restart succeeds on the retry.
plan: Add DC.api, DC.stream and DC.poll to web/src/core.js.
Remove the demo-only window.claude decision store; keep localStorage.
Keep the blueprint layer and the tours.
Let a wired page call DC.markSample(false); unwired pages keep the 'Sample data' pill.
Exercise a write after restarting the server.

decisions.decision: Pages are wired phase by phase; an unwired page keeps its sample and says so.
decisions.why: A page half-filled with real and sample numbers would mislead; the pill tells the user which they see.

decisions.decision: The top-bar pill reads 'Your data' on a wired page instead of disappearing.
decisions.why: Saying positively what is shown is clearer than an absent label.

change: core.js gained the server helpers (api with the CSRF token, server-sent events, polling) and lost the artifact-only shared decision store; DC.markSample toggles the pill.

findings.defect: After a server restart, an open page failed every action until it was reloaded.
findings.scenario: With the product open in the browser, the server restarted (a new request token); every write from the page was refused with 403 and kept failing until the user reloaded.
findings.cause: The page cached the token from its first load and never refreshed it.
findings.fix: On a refused write the page fetches a fresh token from /api/config once and retries the request.
findings.test: Checked in the browser after a restart while wiring the connectors.
findings.impact: After any routine restart (a reload in development, a crash, a deploy), every save, upload or run from an open page failed with 403, and nothing on screen said a reload would fix it. To a user the product looked broken.
findings.open: Any 403 on a write is now retried once after fetching /api/config again, including a refusal for another reason, such as a role that may not make the move once sign-in arrived in 10.2. The second answer is the one shown, so the cost is one extra request, not a wrong result; reads are not retried.

outcome: Done: every wired page goes through DC.api, DC.stream and DC.poll; a write after a restart succeeds on the retry.
lessons: A cached credential needs one refresh path; without it, a routine restart looks like a broken product.
risks: The CSRF token is cached by the page and changes on every server restart, so every write from an open page fails until a reload.
A page mixing real numbers and demo samples misleads unless each page says which it shows.
Removing the demo's window.claude decision store breaks any page or tour that still calls it.
A server-sent event stream that drops on a network blip leaves the page silently out of date unless it reconnects.
Retrying a refused write could send a request twice if the first one had in fact been applied.
